newsitem.title: USA: EMU stability rules near, caveats an issue - Belgium.
newsitem.headline: EMU stability rules near, caveats an issue - Belgium.

text.p: European ministers have agreed nearly all points of a budget stability pact, though the definition of exceptional circumstances which would provide exemptions under the pact remains a difficult issue, Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Tuesday.

"In Dublin we agreed on practically everything about the stability pact. The most difficult issue is how we define exceptional circumstances which would justify countries having a deficit exceeding three percent of GDP," he told Reuters in an interview.

EU finance ministers agreed in principle at a meeting in Dublin last month on a budget stability pact which will commit members of European monetary union to maintain their deficits below three percent of gross domestic product even after the launch of a single currency in 1999.

Under the pact, monetary union members will aim to hold their budgets close to balance over the medium-term, but will be allowed to increase deficits to up to three percent of GDP if economic slowdown justifies it.

Maystadt said "there was a sense of consensus" among EU finance ministers to support proposals by the European Commission which would fine countries 0.2 percent of GDP if their deficits overshot, rising according to the increase in the deficit, with a ceiling on the fine of 0.5 percent.
But he said it was extremely difficult to define the "temporary and exceptional circumstances" which would exempt monetary union members from such fines.
Germany has suggested these should be defined as a contraction of two percent in the economy.
Maystadt said, however, that natural disasters such as earthquakes, might also knock a country off course.

"We should try to define (exceptional circumstances) as precisely as possible, but I'm not sure it is possible to define exactly in advance. It's not possible to define the magnitude of disasters," he said.

The European Union's monetary committee is due to try to work out details on the stability pact over the next few months with the aim of getting approval by EU leaders at a summit meeting in Dublin in December.
